up: Retrieve IC50 activities in nM against target CHEMBL284 (Dipeptidyl peptidase 4). For each activity, return canonical SMILES, compound ChEMBL ID, compound key, PubMed ID or DOI, assay description, standard_type, standard_relation, standard_value, standard_units, activity_comment, target ChEMBL ID, target name, and target organism. Keep only rows where target_type is 'SINGLE PROTEIN', organism is 'Homo sapiens', canonical_smiles is not null, and at least one of pubmed_id or doi is present. For the PubMed ID or DOI field, prefer pubmed_id when both are present; otherwise use doi. Join docs from activities.doc_id = docs.doc_id, and left join compound_records from activities.record_id = compound_records.record_id only to obtain compound_key. Return distinct rows across the output columns; do not emit duplicate projected rows from many-to-many joins.
sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  md.chembl_id AS compound_chembl_id,
  cs.canonical_smiles,
  cr.compound_key,
  COALESCE(docs.pubmed_id, docs.doi) AS pubmed_id_or_doi,
  ass.description AS assay_description,
  act.standard_type,
  act.standard_relation,
  act.standard_value,
  act.standard_units,
  act.activity_comment,
  td.chembl_id AS target_chembl_id,
  td.pref_name AS target_name,
  td.organism AS target_organism
FROM activities act
JOIN assays ass ON act.assay_id = ass.assay_id
JOIN target_dictionary td ON ass.tid = td.tid
JOIN molecule_dictionary md ON act.molregno = md.molregno
JOIN compound_structures cs ON md.molregno = cs.molregno
JOIN docs ON act.doc_id = docs.doc_id
LEFT JOIN compound_records cr ON act.record_id = cr.record_id
WHERE
  td.chembl_id = 'CHEMBL284'
  AND td.target_type = 'SINGLE PROTEIN'
  AND td.organism = 'Homo sapiens'
  AND act.standard_type = 'IC50'
  AND act.standard_units = 'nM'
  AND cs.canonical_smiles IS NOT NULL
  AND (docs.pubmed_id IS NOT NULL OR docs.doi IS NOT NULL);
